_comment: Review rule for the /imps code-review gate (scripts/run-ocr.sh).
OCR has no severity field in its output — every comment is just {path, line, body}.
The imps review contract requires one, so the rule below instructs the reviewer to
prefix each comment with [blocker], [major], [minor] or [nit]; run-ocr.sh parses that
prefix off the body. An untagged comment is treated as `major`, so a model that
ignores this instruction blocks the run rather than silently passing it.
Rule order is significant: FIRST MATCH WINS. The catch-all must stay last.

rules.rule: Shell review. Start every comment with [blocker], [major], [minor] or [nit]. Prioritise: unquoted expansions that break on spaces or globs; `set -e` assumptions that do not hold inside pipelines, command substitutions or `if` conditions; exit codes swallowed by a pipe; temp files created without cleanup traps; and secrets reaching argv or logs. Do not comment on style a formatter would fix.

JavaScript/TypeScript review. Start every comment with [blocker], [major], [minor] or [nit]. Prioritise: unawaited promises; errors caught and discarded; state mutated across async boundaries; and control flow that can return without satisfying its documented contract. Do not comment on formatting.

Python review. Start every comment with [blocker], [major], [minor] or [nit]. Prioritise: exceptions caught too broadly; mutable default arguments; iteration over a structure being modified; and I/O whose failure mode is a silent empty result rather than an error. Do not comment on formatting.

YAML/workflow review. Start every comment with [blocker], [major], [minor] or [nit]. Prioritise: GitHub Actions expressions evaluated in a context where they are empty; permissions broader than the job needs; secrets exposed to untrusted triggers; and job-level conditions that silently skip rather than fail. Do not comment on indentation.

Documentation review. Start every comment with [blocker], [major], [minor] or [nit]. Comment only where the prose contradicts the code in this same diff, documents a flag or path that does not exist, or states a factual claim the diff disproves. Do not comment on wording, tone or structure.

Start every comment with [blocker], [major], [minor] or [nit]. A [blocker] or [major] must name a concrete breaking input or scenario AND a concrete fix — if you cannot name both, it is at most [minor]. Judge the diff against the acceptance criteria supplied as background. Do not manufacture findings: returning no comments is the correct output for a clean diff.
